main_text.head: SECT. VIII.
De Accentibus.
main_text.p: Apud Syros semper omittuntur accentuum notae: quae autem syllaba inter legendum tono affici debeat, ex hisce regulis observare licet.

1 In diffyllabis, si prima syllaba efferatur per Scheva quiescens, vocalis Scheva illud antecedens accentum habet, ut, [illegible, ~5 letters] málcho Rex: si secunda, tunc illa afficitur, ut [illegible, ~5 letters] halécḥ ivit: si utraque sic se habeat, at utraque afficitur, ut [illegible, ~6 letters] lémdéth didici. Si neutra habeat scheva quiescens, prima afficitur, ut [illegible, ~5 letters] kthóvo liber.
2 In trisyllabis, secunda plerunque afficitur, ut in [illegible, ~8 letters] mazmúro psalmus.
3 In quadrisyllabis, &c.: penultima afficitur, ut [illegible, ~9 letters] martyonútho admonitio.
main_text.head: SECT. IX.
De Distinctionibus.
main_text.p: Distinctionum notas habent Syri, puncto uno crassiori, vel duobus, vel asterisco adhibitis, quae incisa, colon, vel periodum de-fignant

page.notes: The Syriac words (vowel-pointed script with accent marks above and below) could not be read letter by letter, so each is marked illegible with an approximate letter count. The transliterations printed beside them (málcho, halécḥ, lémdéth, kthóvo, mazmúro, martyonútho) are copied as printed. The "ḥ" in halécḥ is uncertain. "&c." is copied as printed. The "Sect. IX" paragraph's opening line is set fuller, and "fignant" is printed as a catchword at the right of the last line.
